rules.statement: Never write a secret, token, authorization code or request query string into an audit record; record an identifier or a hash instead.
rules.why: Audit records are persisted and indexed, and a query string can carry codes or tokens.
rules.check: Look for audit record or details writers that emit token values, secrets, codes, `Request.QueryString`, `Request.Query` or full URLs.

rules.statement: Report an audit failure with a required machine-readable error code (for example an OAuth error code), with any prose only as a separate message field, never as a free-text reason alone.
rules.why: Investigators need a field to group failures on, such as every failed client authentication for one error.
rules.check: Look for audit errors or failure events built without a code, or that put only prose into a reason or message field.

rules.statement: Have each event write its event-specific audit details through a typed writer method (e.g. `WriteAuditDetails(Utf8JsonWriter)`), not through an `IDictionary<string, object>` bag or a `[JsonExtensionData]` member.
rules.why: A dynamic bag lets any value, including a secret, reach a persisted record, and it invites magic-string keys instead of reviewed typed fields. It also is not trimming- or AOT-safe.
rules.check: Look for dictionary or object bags, or `[JsonExtensionData]`, used to carry audit or event details.

rules.statement: Declare telemetry field names once as constants and use those same names in the audit record, the log state, the span tags and the metric attributes.
rules.why: An operator can only pivot from a log entry to its trace or metric when the same event uses the same names in every signal.
rules.check: Look for string-literal field or tag names in log, span or metric code that duplicate or differ from the shared field-name constants.

rules.statement: Do not log a structured record as one serialized JSON string property; emit its fields as separate flattened key/value attributes, with numbers kept as numbers.
rules.why: A collector cannot index or filter on fields inside one opaque string without parsing it first.
rules.check: Look for logging calls that pass `JsonSerializer.Serialize(...)` output or a raw JSON string as a single log property for data that should be indexed.

rules.statement: Use only bounded fields (for example event name, category and outcome) as metric attributes, never identifiers such as tenant, subject, client or trace ids.
rules.why: Metric dimensions must stay bounded, so high-cardinality values do not belong on metrics.
rules.check: Look for metric tags or attributes that take ids, user agents, IP addresses or other unbounded values.

rules.statement: Generate audit event identifiers with `Guid.CreateVersion7()`, not `Guid.NewGuid()`.
rules.why: UUIDv7 identifiers are time-ordered, so they index and paginate well.
rules.check: Look for `Guid.NewGuid()` used to create audit or event record ids.

rules.statement: Write record timestamps as UTC in RFC 3339 form with a `Z` suffix.
rules.why: The record's event time must be an unambiguous UTC instant that operators can index.
rules.check: Look for local-time values, offsets other than Z, or custom date formats in audit record timestamps.

rules.statement: Write JSON records to buffer writers or pooled buffers and never allocate an intermediate `byte[]`; when the destination is a ref struct writer, stage the record in a pooled buffer and copy it.
rules.why: The memory-allocation conventions forbid `byte[]` allocations in writers, and `Utf8JsonWriter` cannot hold a ref struct.
rules.check: Look for `ToArray()`, `new byte[]` or `JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes` in record-writing paths.

rules.statement: Parse a JSON record you read back with `JsonElement.Parse`, not `JsonDocument.Parse`.
rules.why: The decision says a record is read back as a `JsonElement`, which avoids a disposable `JsonDocument` with pooled memory.
rules.check: Look for `JsonDocument.Parse` used to read back written records.

rules.statement: When code calls `ILogger.Log` directly as an approved exception to the `[LoggerMessage]`-only rule, add a `//` comment at the call that cites the decision allowing it.
rules.why: The source generator does not check the keys of a direct call, so the exception has to be visible and justified where it is made.
rules.check: Look for direct `ILogger.Log`/`LogInformation`-style calls that have no comment citing the decision that permits them.

rules.statement: Never reuse a retired or reserved log `EventId` number for a new log message.
rules.why: Stable event ids let operators filter logs, and reusing a reserved id would mix unrelated entries.
rules.check: Look for new log event ids that collide with ids marked as reserved or retired.

rules.statement: Bump the record's single schema minor version when you add a field to a versioned record envelope, and do not give individual event types their own schema versions.
rules.why: One version string for the whole record tells consumers which shape they are reading.
rules.check: Look for new envelope fields with no change to the schema version constant, or for per-event version properties.

rules.statement: Leave out record members that have no value, and leave out empty arrays, instead of writing null or `[]`.
rules.why: The record format omits a member without a value, and omits empty resources.
rules.check: Look for writers that emit null values or empty arrays for optional record members.

rules.statement: Capture HTTP request context for an event when the event is published, not inside a sink that may run in the background after the request has completed.
rules.why: Background delivery can run after the request has completed, when `HttpContext` is no longer valid.
rules.check: Look for event handlers or sinks that read `HttpContext` or `IHttpContextAccessor` while delivering events.

rules.statement: Truncate untrusted request header values such as User-Agent to a fixed maximum length (512 characters) before recording them in audit records.
rules.why: The request context records the User-Agent cut at 512 characters, which bounds what a client can inject into the record.
rules.check: Look for User-Agent or other header values copied into records without a length cap.

rules.statement: Do not model an extensible event or record family as a closed polymorphic `[JsonDerivedType]` hierarchy that lists every subtype on the base type.
rules.why: Vocabularies are open, so a package that adds an event must not have to edit the base library.
rules.check: Look for `[JsonDerivedType]` attributes that enumerate event types on a shared base event or record type.

rules.statement: Keep event and audit abstractions packages free of ASP.NET Core HTTP types, and put HTTP-dependent factories in an HTTP-aware package.
rules.why: The events abstractions package has to stay independent of HTTP.
rules.check: Look for `HttpContext` or `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http` references added to events or audit abstraction projects.
